title: Customer QBR Rapid Roundhouse Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, high-velocity QBR facilitation playbook designed for accounts where executive alignment + clear renewal signals are needed quickly. The "Rapid Roundhouse" format compresses a strategic QBR into a tightly-moderated 20–45 minute session that surfaces the critical signals, clarifies decisions, and leaves with concrete, time-bound commitments.

When to use this playbook:
- Customer renewal window < 90 days and cross-functional stakeholders are busy
- A technical incident or recent launch changed adoption trends and we need fast sync
- Internal alignment required across CS, Solutions Engineering, and Product with limited calendar availability

Core structure (3-round framework):
1) Signals (data + progress) — What the data says (6–12 min)
2) Decisions (asks + options) — What we need to decide now (6–12 min)
3) Actions (owners + timing) — Commitments and follow-ups (6–12 min)

Attendees & roles (keep lean):
- Facilitator (CS lead) — runs timing, asks explicit decision questions, captures actions
- Product/Engineering SME (optional, on-call) — answers technical constraints or roadmap questions
- Customer Exec Sponsor (1) — business owner who signs to renew
- Customer Technical Lead (1) — adoption and integration owner
- Solutions/SE (optional) — if a technical change is a potential ask
- Note-taker (rotating) — capture actions, owners, deadlines, and links to artifacts

Pre-meeting (preflight) checklist — required prep (Facilitator + CS AE):
- Pull last 90-day usage summary (MAUs, token/transaction volume, feature adoption) — attach CSV or screenshot
- Errors/availability: past 90-day incidents and current open tickets (Jira IDs)
- ROI signals: evidence of business impact or cost avoidance (short bullets)
- Contract & renewal window, T&Cs that matter for this account (dates, notice windows)
- Current open expansion or risk opportunities (value estimate, stage)
- Recommended ask(s) to present at the meeting (primary + fallback)
- Share 1-page pre-read to customer 48 hours before the meeting (title: "Rapid Roundhouse: Account Signals & Asks")

Optional: Preflight template to paste in invite as a short agenda and expectations:
"30 min | Rapid Roundhouse QBR — Please review attached 1-page. Goal: agree on renewal path or define a 14-day decision plan. Bring one example of outcome from last 90d (usage or ROI)."

Run-of-show — 30-minute variant (timestamps are wall-clock)
- 0:00–0:02 — Quick framing by Facilitator: objective and timebox
  Script: "Thanks everyone. We’ll run a focused 30-minute checkpoint: 3 rounds — Signals, Decisions, Actions. I’ll call time so we leave with owners and dates."
- 0:02–0:12 — Signals round (10m) — Facilitator narrates top 3 signals; customer confirms/clarifies
  Script prompts: "Top signals for Redwood: (1) adoption velocity (2) reliability/ops incidents (3) realized value. Do you see anything different on your side?"
- 0:12–0:20 — Decisions round (8m) — Present the ask(s) and options; solicit customer preference
  Script prompts: "Option A: 12-month renewal at committed reserved capacity. Option B: 6-month bridge with dedicated support and growth review. Which aligns with your procurement timeline?"
- 0:20–0:28 — Actions round (8m) — Assign owners, set deadlines, and capture dependencies
  Script: "Maya (CS) will deliver contract language by Thursday. Customer procurement to confirm internal sign-off by next Wed. SE to scope migration work in 48 hours."
- 0:28–0:30 — Rapid close — confirm attendees, next sync cadence, and populate action tracker

20-minute variant (very urgent) — compress Signals to 4m, Decisions to 8m, Actions to 6m; reserve 2m close.
45-minute variant (expanded) — expand Signals to 18m with deeper operational readout and one breakout for technical deep-dive if needed.

Facilitation cues & scripts (concise):
- Silence is a tool: after the ask, pause 5–7s for customer to respond — don’t fill the gap
- Explicit decision-first framing: "What decision do we need from you today?"
- Two-option pattern: always present a primary and fallback to avoid open-ended conversation
- Time-box redirection phrase: "We have 5 minutes left for Decisions — let’s pick the option that keeps momentum and capture follow-ups for detail work."
- If conversation drifts technical: "Great deep-dive — can we capture that as a 30–45m follow-up with SE and schedule it? For this meeting we need decision X."

Escalation and fallback lanes (if no decision):
- Customer asks for more time: set a firm date no >14 calendar days; define what the missing artifact is and who will deliver it
- Procurement stall: identify procurement contact and schedule a 15-min procurement-only call in next 3 business days
- Technical blocker: SE to produce a compatibility note within 48 hours and propose mitigation or timeline

Action tracker (paste this into meeting notes or shared tracker):
Columns: Action | Owner | Due date | Status | Artifact/Link
Sample rows: "Finalize renewal terms" | "Maya Chen" | "2025-02-22" | "In progress" | "confluence:acct-xyz/renewal-draft"
"SE scope migration" | "Jordan Lee" | "2025-02-20" | "Todo" | "JIRA:CSUP-4210"

Templates to use after the meeting:
- Post-meeting subject line (email): "[Account] | Rapid Roundhouse — Decisions, Actions (due dates inside)"
- Short post-meeting summary (one paragraph + bulleted tasks): paste into CRM and attach action tracker link
- If customer needs internal approval: one-pager with the preferred option, win themes, and procurement ask (we own production)

Risk signals to call out during Signals round (examples):
- 15% drop in active usage over last 30 days with no mapped business event
- Critical SEV incidents in last 60 days with unresolved RCA commitments
- Procurement change or consolidation that affects approval thresholds
- Overage charges trending >10% month-over-month without commitment

Renewal decision heuristics (helpful facilitator checklist):
- Customer demonstrates a clear owner willing to sign or set a procurement date
- There is a path to close within 14 days or an agreed 30-day escalation plan with named stakeholders
- The Ask we present has a fallback that preserves revenue and gives time for technical work

Short library of canned phrases for often-seen outcomes:
- If customer signs: "Great — we’ll kick off paperwork and schedule a 30-minute implementation check-in for Day 7."
- If customer needs more data: "We’ll deliver the usage ROI pack and a one-pager on E2E reliability by EOD +2."
- If customer stalls: "We’ll set a procurement-only 15-minute call and escalate to your sponsor if there is no response in 7 days."

Post-meeting hygiene (CS lead responsibilities within 24 hours):
- Publish 2-paragraph summary and paste action tracker to CRM and Confluence
- Create follow-up meetings (procurement call / SE scope call) with owners and deadlines
- Notify Deal Desk or Legal if contract language change required
- Flag Renewal as "at-risk" or "on-track" in the internal tracker and set a 7-day review cadence if at-risk

Appendix: Example 1-page pre-read outline (single slide/doc):
- Title: Rapid Roundhouse — [Account] — 30m
- One-line objective: e.g., "Agree on renewal path or define a 14-day decision plan."
- Top 3 signals (bulleted with data points)
- Recommended ask(s) with two options and our recommended option highlighted
- Known blockers and what we need from customer today
- Proposed next steps and owners

Notes & open questions to iterate in this playbook:
- Add a short checklist for seats vs token billing models (account-specific economics)
- Consider an automated preflight pack generated from usage dashboards
- Add a short template for Enterprise Legal escalations with standard terms suggested to speed renewals

Last updated by Maya Chen — contact: maya@redwood.ai
summary: Compact facilitation playbook for 20–45m QBRs (Rapid Roundhouse), with preflight checklist, run-of-show, scripts, escalation lanes, action tracker template, and post-meeting hygiene.
